issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose commercial tenancy continues only under statutory protection after the lease ends cannot bequeath the right to occupy the premises to a legatee who does not meet the statutory qualification for succession.
material_facts: The premises had been let for business, and the tenant continued to have a right to occupy them only under statutory protection after the contractual tenancy ended.
Before her death, the tenant bequeathed the tenancy right to the claimant.
The claimant was not a member of the tenant’s family carrying on business with her in the premises at the time of her death.
The landlord sought possession, and the claimant relied on the will to assert a right to remain in the premises.
issues.conclusion: The bequest did not make the claimant a tenant because he did not satisfy the statutory qualification; the landlord was not required to treat him as a tenant, and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(11)(c)(ii) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, the right to a protected tenancy in premises let for business, trade or storage devolves only on a qualifying member of the tenant’s family, subject to the stated conditions; the provision does not authorize a testamentary bequest to another person. Section 15(1) prohibits a tenant, absent a contract to the contrary, from assigning or transferring the tenant’s interest, and the Court approved Dr. Anant Triamback Sabnis v. Vasant Pratap Pandit, which treated a bequest as within that prohibition. Gian Devi v. Jeevan Kumar concerned intestate succession and a different statute that did not restrict succession to commercial tenancies, so it did not support the legatee’s claim; Jaspal Singh v. The Additional District Judge, Bulandshahr was also referred to in considering restrictions on transferring tenancy rights. The Court left open the wider question whether a statutory tenancy personal to a tenant can ever be bequeathed.

rule.if: commercial_tenancy_after_lease_termination and tenant_bequeathed_occupancy_right and legatee_not_qualifying_family_member and landlord_seeks_possession

predicates.commercial_tenancy_after_lease_terminati: The tenant occupied premises let for business, trade, or storage under statutory protection after the contractual tenancy ended.
predicates.tenant_bequeathed_occupancy_right: The tenant purported to leave the right to occupy the premises to another person by will.
predicates.legatee_not_qualifying_family_member: The legatee was not a member of the tenant’s family carrying on the relevant business, trade, or storage with the tenant in the premises at the tenant’s death and continuing it afterward.
predicates.landlord_seeks_possession: The landlord sought possession from the person claiming the tenancy under the will.

issues.definition: When a tenant occupying commercial premises under statutory protection after the lease ends bequeaths the occupancy right to a person who does not meet the qualifying-family-member condition, and the landlord seeks possession, that person cannot acquire the tenancy by bequest.
